summary: The shell enforces Screen Time limits and Downtime itself. Apps can read only whether child restrictions are on. There is no app-facing settings store, no tokens for apps or categories, and no family-account service.
rea_evidence: not captured: REA capture pending (tools/parity/rea-page.sh not run in this batch); facts are from tools/parity/docc.py

features.note: apps can read whether restrictions are enforced and observe changes; they cannot write restrictions

features.apple: Screen Time settings applied by the system
features.note: per-app daily limits and Downtime are set in the shell and counted from app usage; no framework for other apps to call
no privacy-preserving token for an app, category or site

features.apple: Manage settings on devices in a Family Sharing group
features.note: depends on the Apple Family Sharing account service; BifrOSt has no such service

features.apple: Confirming the effective TV and movie ratings
features.note: needs Apple's content rating data; no rating feed exists on the port

gaps: No app-facing store that applies restrictions to the device or to other apps.
No tokens that name an app, a category or a website without revealing it.
Restrictions are shell-only; no third-party app can enforce its own limits through an API.
